messages:
kevin: fyi i sketched an autoscale-aware fallback idea for canaries. goal: avoid full swap -> use 'soft fallback' first (quantized / smaller variant, or regional redirect) when we see capacity pressure. want API + console bits to control it.

maya: short summary of signals and actions?

kevin: signals: GPU_free_pct < 15% OR request_queue_ms_p50 > 1200 OR p95 latency > 1.5s. actions in order: 1) route X% of canary -> cheaper-quantized variant, 2) route remainder to region B (if healthy), 3) if both fail, reduce canary weight to 0 and revert to stable. also optional: degrade output (temperature/hallucination guard) for cheaper variant.

ash: hmm cheaper-quantized variant could change outputs a lot. we need a telemetry guard for 'semantic drift' (eval set token-level similarity / answer correctness). can't just rely on latency/cost.

amanda: agreed. propose attaching a tiny eval harness in canary: sample 1/500 requests -> run eval function that checks gold prompts or a diff-based metric. if drift > threshold, immediate cut.

kevin: yeah that was the plan. we can ship a "mini-eval" event type. console shows mini-eval pass/fail rate + sample diffs.

maya: UX question: should the fallback policy be a first-class object on rollout config or a global policy with per-rollout overrides?

ash: leaning global default + per-rollout override. global keeps sane defaults; per-rollout overrides for risky models.

amanda: cost control perspective -> we should add a "budget" knob on rollouts: monthly_budget_cents and per-minute_burst_cents. soft fallback prioritizes staying under budget.

kevin: idea for API shape: rollout.fallbacks = [{"trigger":{"metric":"GPU_free_pct","op":"lt","value":15},"action":{"type":"swap_variant","variant":"quantized-8bit","traffic_pct":30}}, {"trigger":{"metric":"mini_eval_fail_rate","op":"gt","value":0.1},"action":{"type":"cut_weight","value":0}}]  // accept feedback on naming

ash: love structured triggers. add time window (eval over 5m) + cooldown to avoid flip-flopping. also need circuit-breaker metric for "user_visible_errors" like 5xx or aborted streams.

maya: console: show an inline preview of fallback chain for a rollout: a small diagram + expected latency/cost impact. ops should be able to manually advance to next fallback step.

kevin: also propose a "soft mode" flag to do a percentage pseudo-fallback (proxy path that annotates responses with fallback=true) so we can compare outputs in prod without user impact.

amanda: telemetry: we need these time series for dashboards: canary_weight, fallback_active, mini_eval_fail_rate, p95_latency, gpu_free_pct, regional_error_rate. also traces with tags for "fallback-step".

ash: how do we prioritize regional failover vs quantized variant? some customers prefer same-region always. need policy param order: prefer_variant vs prefer_region.

kevin: right — rollout.fallbacks can be ordered list, but also a preference key. default: prefer_variant (cheaper, same-region), fallback: prefer_region for data locality customers.

amanda: SLA implications: if fallback moves traffic to another region, we must surface latency delta and get product approval for cross-region failover. add agreement checkbox in console for that option.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: update rollout-controller with fallback-first prototype (branch: rollout/fallback-soft-2026). CI: 1 test failing (timeout).

kevin: i'll fix the test. also need to add canary-level sampling hook for mini-eval.

ash: for ops: add an alert rule: fallback_active == true && mini_eval_fail_rate > 0.05 for 3m -> page oncall. otherwise page only on full-cut.

maya: any objections to exposing mini-eval sample content in logs? privacy concerns for PII. must sample and redact.

amanda: yep redact + opt-out for customers serving regulated data. default off for private deployments.

kevin: next steps: i'll open RFC PR with API examples, console mockups, sample metrics, and a small runbook for canary owners. aim to ship prototype to staging next week.

ash: ping me on the RFC; i'll add the alarm rules + circuit-breaker logic.

amanda: i'll scope dashboard tiles and budget enforcement flow.

kevin: thanks all :thumbsup:
